cues.text: Section eight: Standards and governance.
Let us begin with ISO 22301.
This standard specifies the requirements for a business continuity management system, often shortened to BCMS.
It supports a number of areas: organisational context, leadership, planning, implementation, performance evaluation, and continual improvement.
An important practical point is that organisations can seek certification against its requirements.
Next, NIST Special Publication 800-34.
This document provides contingency planning guidance for information systems.

Its approach includes the following elements, in order: policy, the business impact analysis, or BIA, preventive controls, contingency strategies, plan development, testing, training and exercises, and finally maintenance.
Notice the contrast with the previous standard.
NIST guidance is not the same as ISO certification.
NIST gives guidance you can follow, whereas ISO 22301 is something an organisation can be certified against.
Now consider ISO/IEC 27001.
This standard addresses information security management, and it complements continuity planning.
The two must be coordinated.
In practice, this means that recovery should not restore compromised systems, and it should not bypass access controls.
A fast recovery that brings back a compromised system, or that skips access controls to save time, defeats the purpose of both disciplines.
Let us turn to the financial sector.
Financial institutions face operational resilience expectations because payment disruption can affect customers and the wider economy.

The Basel operational resilience principles emphasise several areas: governance, operational risk management, continuity testing, dependency mapping, third-party management, incident management, and resilient ICT.
Be careful here.
Basel III is primarily a prudential capital and liquidity framework, so do not confuse it with the separate operational resilience principles.
Also relevant is the SWIFT Customer Security Programme, which supports the security of relevant financial messaging environments.
Finally, remember that applicable obligations depend on the institution and the jurisdiction.
Nigerian organisations, in particular, must consider relevant sector regulators, data protection obligations, and local infrastructure constraints.
